- oiml_issuer_id: not present explicitly... "The notification of NMi Certin as Issuing Authority can be verified at www.oiml.org." No ID number. Omit.

- name: NMi Certin B.V.
- address_lines: ["Hugo de Grootplein 1", "3314 EG Dordrecht", "The Netherlands"] — also P.O. Box in footer: "P.O. Box 394, 3300 AJ Dordrecht, NL". I'll include the main address lines. Maybe include P.O. box too? The address block is "Hugo de Grootplein 1, 3314 EG Dordrecht, The Netherlands". Keep those three lines.
- person_responsible: Ing. C. Oosterman
- person_title: Manager Product Certification

Manufacturer: same.

Certified type:
- category: "Load cell"
- type_designations: ["SSP1260"]
- module_designation: "Analog load cell"? The cert says "A bending beam load cell". Module designation per R60 would be "Analog load cell" — but it's not explicitly stated. Better to leave null or omit. Actually the description: "A bending beam load cell, Type SSP1260, Fraction Pi = 0.7, Temperature range -10°C/+40°C". Hmm. The schema has module_designation: "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. Since not stated, set null or omit. I'll set null.

Characteristics type_level:
- fraction_of_maximum_capacity_verification_interval? "Fraction: Pi = 0.7" → attribute fraction_plc or p_i. Rule example: apportionment factor pLC → apportionment_factor_plc. For load cells, p_i (fraction) → "fraction_pi" or "apportionment_factor_pi". I'll use "fraction_pi" with value 0.7. Actually the R60 term is "fraction of the maximum permissible error p_i". Canonical: "fraction_p_i"? Rule 1 says snake_case canonical labels. Let me use "fraction_pi" value 0.7, unit null. Hmm, maybe "apportionment_factor_pi". The example given: "Apportionment factor pLC" → "apportionment_factor_plc". So "Fraction Pi = 0.7" → "fraction_pi" value 0.7. I'll go with "fraction_pi".

- temperature_range: value {min: -10, max: 40}, unit_symbol: "°C"
- maximum_capacity: "150 kg up to and including 750 kg" → this is a range: 150 to 750 kg. Per matrix rule: is this a model matrix? "150 kg up to and including 750 kg" — it's a range of Emax for the certified type, meaning multiple variants with Emax between 150 and 750 kg. In NMi certs like this, the load cell covers Emax from 150 to 750 kg — capacities within the range. This is a range, not a discrete list. So type_level with value {min: 150, max: 750}, unit "kg". Hmm, but Rule 4 says lists of values (25,30,50,60,75,90) are model matrices. Here it's a continuous range "150 kg up to and including 750 kg". Treat as range: {min: 150, max: 750}, unit_symbol "kg". Attribute name: maximum_capacity.

- accuracy_class: "C" → string "C".
- maximum_number_of_load_cell_intervals_n: 3000, unit null (dimensionless, "intervals" — unit could be null). Rule example says max_load_cell_intervals_nlc. Here it's "(n)" not nLC. Use "maximum_number_of_load_cell_intervals_n", value 3000.
- ratio_y_emax_over_vmin: 7500.

Recommendation:
- id: "R60", edition: 2000, amendment: null, scheme: null (not stated; OIML-CS scheme... The cert number contains NL1; scheme not mentioned). accuracy_classes: ["C"].

Test reports:
- R60/2000-NL-02.12, 40 pages, role type_evaluation_report
- R60/2000-NL1-07.14, 40 pages, role type_evaluation_report
Also "test certificate and the description with number TC6043 and the appertaining documentation folder" → documentation_file: TC6043. Add test_reports entry: {id: "TC6043", role: "documentation_file"}. Date/pages not present → omit.

Revision history: not present.

Footnotes: none.

Model family: Should I include? The cert covers a range of Emax 150–750 kg, which is a family of capacities but no discrete models listed. The schema says include model_family ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. Here it's a continuous range, not discrete variants. I could omit model_family. But characteristics vary within the range (n=3000 given overall). I'll omit model_family and keep maximum_capacity as a range at type_level. That seems right per the example rules — the R60 example in rules was for comma-separated discrete values. Here "150 kg up to and including 750 kg" is a range → min/max.

Date issued: 23 November 2007 → "2007-11-23".

Scheme: OIML-CS scheme A vs B. This is a 2007 NMi certificate (pre-OIML-CS?). OIML-CS started 2017. But schema demands scheme (A|B). The traditional certificate of conformity corresponds to scheme A. I'll put "A".

date_issued format: ISO "2007-11-23".
